chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), regarding the egg of the sandgrouse, is a young sheep; when the one in Ihram attains it, similar to what is regarding the egg of the ostrich, a young she-camel.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: the one in Ihram (state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for killing a sandgrouse or ostrich while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the specific expiation (*kaffarah*) for killing birds while in Ihram, citing the *Musnad* of Imam Ali (AS) to differentiate penalties based on the bird's size and value. It highlights the juristic principle of analogical reasoning (*qiyas*) by equating the sandgrouse (*qat*) with the ostrich (*na'ama*) in terms of their respective sacrificial animals—a young sheep and a young camel, respectively. This ruling underscores the precision of Shia fiqh in maintaining the sanctity of the sacred state by linking the severity of the act to the value of the offering.
